header.title: GradientText
header.description: Gradient fill on text using `background-clip: text`. The root is a `span`, so it fits in any line of text. The gradient is painted on an inner `span` (the surface) and the glyph fill turns transparent to let it through. `variant` sets the motion: `flow` slides the gradient across the glyphs, `static` keeps it fixed, and `pulse` makes the brightness breathe.

playground.title: Playground
playground.description: Combine the props and see the code they generate. With `static`, `trigger` changes nothing: the gradient always shows.
playground.label: Gradient

base.title: Basic text
base.description: With the defaults (`variant="flow"`, `angle={110}`, `duration={3200}`), a `primary-400`, `secondary-400`, and `tertiary-400` gradient slides back and forth across the glyphs.

variants.title: Variants
variants.description: `flow` slides the gradient from one end to the other and back. `static` keeps it fixed, fitted to the text width. `pulse` keeps it fixed and makes brightness, saturation, and opacity breathe.

heading.title: On a heading
heading.description: The typical use: a featured heading. Since the root is a `span`, use `asChild` on a block heading: the `h2` stays the root and its content is wrapped in the surface. The gradient is clipped to all the text, children included, even when they set their own `color`.

inline.title: Inside a paragraph
inline.description:
The root is a `span`, so you can highlight a few words inside a `

` without invalid HTML. Its base layout has zero specificity: here a class puts it back on the text line (`vertical-align: baseline`).

texts.after: and respect your design system's tokens.

colors.title: Colors
colors.description: `from`, `via`, and `to` are the gradient's three stops. Defaults: gem-system's `primary-400`, `secondary-400`, and `tertiary-400`. Prefer tokens.

angle.title: Angle
angle.description: `angle` is the gradient's direction: a number is degrees, and any `linear-gradient` value works too, such as `"to top right"`. It's most visible with `static`.

triggers.title: Triggers
triggers.description: With `hover` the text uses the inherited color and the gradient appears when the pointer enters (or something inside gets keyboard focus). With `click`, each click shows or hides it. The animation restarts every time.

intensity.title: Intensity
intensity.description: With `flow`, `intensity` sets how far the gradient travels: the background is `160%`, `220%`, or `300%` of the text with `sm`, `md`, or `lg`, so higher intensity shows a smaller slice and a wider motion. With `pulse`, it sets how strongly it breathes: brightness, saturation, and opacity are computed from `--gemfx-gradient-text-intensity`. It also takes a number from `0` to `1`.

duration.title: Duration
duration.description: `duration` is a full cycle of `flow` (one way) or `pulse`, in milliseconds. `delay` postpones the start.

asChild.title: On another element (asChild)
asChild.description: With `asChild`, the gradient is applied to the child without a wrapping `span`: the child is the root and its content is wrapped in an inner `span` (the surface). So the button keeps its background, only the label gets the gradient, and `variant`, `isPaused`, triggers, and states work just like without `asChild`.

state.title: Paused and disabled
state.description: `isPaused` freezes the gradient where it is. `isDisabled` removes it and the text goes back to the inherited color.

callbacks.title: Events
callbacks.description: `onGradientText` fires when the gradient turns on (pointer enter or keyboard focus with `hover`, click with `click`, or mount with `always`) and `outGradientText` when it turns off, with the reason in `event.reason`. With `static` they behave as with `always`. The button sits inside the gradient and keeps a solid label.

header.title: GradientText API
header.description: Reference for the props, inheritance, accessibility, CSS classes and variables, and exported types of `GradientText`.

demos.title: Demos
demos.description: Playground and examples for every variant, trigger, and option.

import.title: Import
import.description: Import it from `@gem-org/gemffects/gradient-text` with its `gradient-text.css`, or from the root if you already load `styles.css`.

inheritance.title: Inheritance
inheritance.body: Accepts HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement> (except color) and passes them to the root span (or to the child, with asChild). onClick, onPointerEnter, onPointerLeave, onFocus, and onBlur run before the effect's internal logic. The --gemfx-gradient-text-* variables of the props you pass are written after style; the ones you don't pass aren't written. The base layout (display, position, vertical-align, color) lives in :where(), so any host class overrides it.

items.reducedMotion: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the gradient stays still, centered and fitted to the text; pulse stops breathing.
items.ignoreReducedMotion: ignoreReducedMotion (or the gemfx-ignore-reduced-motion class on an ancestor) keeps the motion. Only use it when essential.
items.readable: The text is still text: it can be read, selected, and announced by screen readers. The gradient is only a clipped background. Children with their own background (code, kbd, samp, mark, form controls, or .gemfx-gradient-text__solid) go back to a solid color, so their text doesn't turn invisible.
items.selection: The glyph fill is transparent (-webkit-text-fill-color), so when selected you may only see the selection background. If it matters, define a ::selection with its own -webkit-text-fill-color.
items.focus: With trigger="hover" the gradient also appears when the host or something inside gets keyboard focus (:focus-visible), and the events fire just like with the pointer. With click the root isn't focusable: the keyboard only turns it on when the click comes from a control inside.
items.contrast: Check the contrast of every stop against the background, not just the average color: with flow each letter goes through all the colors.

items.root: Root (`span`, or the child with `asChild`). `inline-flex`, `position: relative`, and `color: inherit` live in `:where()` (zero specificity), so a host class overrides them.
items.variant: Active variant. `static` removes the animation and fits the background to the text; `pulse` switches to the brightness animation.
items.trigger: Active trigger, only with `flow` and `pulse`. Sets `cursor: pointer` and removes the gradient while it isn't on.
items.on: Added while the gradient is on with `click`.
items.paused: Added with `isPaused`. Pauses the animation with `animation-play-state`.
items.inactive: Added with `isActive={false}` or `isDisabled`. Removes the gradient and restores the inherited color.
items.surface: Inner `span` that holds the gradient (`background-clip: text`) and the transparent fill. With `asChild` it wraps the child's content, so the child keeps its background.
items.solid: Put it on any descendant to bring back a solid color (`-webkit-text-fill-color: currentcolor`). `code`, `kbd`, `samp`, `mark`, and form controls already do it on their own.

cssVariables.title: CSS variables
cssVariables.description: Only the variables of the props you pass are written inline (`from`, `via`, `to`, `angle`, `intensity`, `duration`, `delay`). When you don't pass the prop, any of them can be overridden from a class.

items.colors: The gradient's three stops. Set by `from`, `via`, and `to`.
items.span: Background width with `flow` (how far it travels). Set by `intensity`: `160%`, `220%`, or `300%`; default `220%`.
items.intensity: Strength of the `pulse` breath (brightness, saturation, and opacity). Set by `intensity`; default `var(--gemfx-intensity-md, 55%)`.

tokens.title: Tokens
tokens.description: Global variables GradientText reads as defaults. You can redefine them on the root with a class.

items.palette: Default colors for `from`, `via`, and `to` (with neon, magenta, and amber fallbacks).
items.intensity: Values for `sm`, `md`, and `lg` (`35%`, `55%`, and `80%`). The `pulse` default uses `md` and the prop writes `var(--gemfx-intensity-*)` for tokens, so redefining them changes the breath.

content.title: Content
content.description: Which text gets the gradient and where the effect mounts.

timing.title: Timing
timing.description: Animation cycle and delay, in milliseconds.

state.title: Trigger and state
state.description: When it shows and moves, how it pauses, and how it turns off.

events.title: Events
events.description: `event.reason` can be `always`, `hover`, `click`, `inactive`, `disabled`, or `unmount`. With `static` they behave as with `always`: `onGradientText` fires on mount.

items.children: Text that gets the gradient. Children with their own background (`code`, `kbd`, `samp`, `mark`, form controls, or `.gemfx-gradient-text__solid`) keep solid text.
items.asChild: Applies the gradient to the single child, without a wrapping `span`. The child's content is wrapped in the surface, so the child keeps its background. Useful for headings and buttons.
items.variant: `flow` slides the gradient, `static` keeps it fixed, and `pulse` makes the brightness breathe.
items.from: First stop. Prefer a token; default `primary-400`.
items.angle: Gradient direction. A number is degrees; any `linear-gradient` value works.
items.intensity: How far the gradient travels with `flow` and how strongly it breathes with `pulse`. Token or number from `0` to `1`.
items.duration: Full `flow` or `pulse` cycle. Negative values become `0`.
items.trigger: `always` shows it all the time, `hover` when the pointer enters or something inside gets keyboard focus, and `click` toggles it on each click. `static` ignores it.
items.isActive: Shows the gradient. With `false` it's removed and `outGradientText` gets `inactive`.
items.isDisabled: Removes the gradient; the text uses the inherited color. `outGradientText` gets `disabled`.
items.ignoreReducedMotion: Keeps the motion even if the user prefers less. Only when essential.
items.onGradientText: Fires when the gradient turns on: on mount with `always` (or `static`), on pointer enter or keyboard focus with `hover`, or on click with `click`.
items.outGradientText: Fires when it turns off: on pointer or focus leave, on the next click, when disabled, or on unmount.
items.classNames: Per-part classes: `root` and `surface` (the inner `span`, also with `asChild`).
items.style: Inline styles for the root. The variables of the props you pass are written after it.
items.ref: Ref to the root (the `span`, or the child with `asChild`).
